$comment: Per-unit learning targets (hs / col), language objectives and sentence frames. Source: OBJ in site/index.html.

hs: I can explain how a message travels from sender to receiver, and name the noise that gets in the way.
I can give a 1–2 minute speech that introduces me with a hook, three clear parts, and a strong ending.
I can explain what plagiarism is and how to give credit out loud.
col: I can compare the linear and transactional models of communication and apply the transactional model to a real speech.
I can deliver a 2–3 minute extemporaneous speech built around a personal artifact, with a clear thesis and three main points.
I can explain the ethical responsibilities of a speaker, including honest use of sources and AI.

lang: I can use the words sender, receiver, message, channel, noise, and feedback to describe a conversation.
I can introduce myself using complete sentences and time-order words (first, then, finally).
I can give a classmate feedback using a sentence frame.
frames: The sender is ___, and the receiver is ___.
One kind of noise was ___ because ___.
I brought ___ because it shows that I ___.
One thing you did well was ___. Next time, try ___.

hs: I can describe my audience and explain how it changes what I say.
I can find three credible sources, including one from Gale, and cite them in APA.
I can write a thesis that previews three main points and build an outline from it.
col: I can conduct an audience analysis (demographic and psychological) and adapt my topic to it.
I can evaluate sources for credibility and locate peer-reviewed research in Gale.
I can write an annotated bibliography and a full-sentence preparation outline in APA 7.

lang: I can explain why a source is or is not credible using because and evidence words.
I can say an oral citation out loud with the author, credentials, and date.
I can write a thesis statement using a preview sentence frame.
frames: Today I will tell you about ___: first ___, second ___, and finally ___.

hs: I can teach my class about an important person’s early life, achievements, challenges, and legacy.
I can use an introduction, transitions, and a conclusion that tie my speech together.
I can design slides with key words and visuals that teach, and cite three sources out loud.
col: I can deliver a 5–7 minute informative speech organized chronologically, with depth and accurate detail.
I can connect a historical figure’s legacy to our community or nation today.
I can integrate five sources, including peer-reviewed research, with oral citations and credentials.

lang: I can use past-tense verbs and time-order transitions to tell a life story (in 19__, later, after that).
I can explain cause and effect using because, as a result, and so.
I can pronounce my person’s name and key terms clearly in English.
frames: One challenge ___ faced was ___. As a result, ___.

hs: I can teach a process in 4–6 clear steps so my audience could repeat it.
I can use real props so everyone can see each step.
I can speak extemporaneously from brief notes.
col: I can organize a demonstration with a clear pattern and signposts, and explain why each step matters.
I can handle props smoothly while staying connected with the whole room.
I can support a demonstration with two credible sources cited aloud.

lang: I can give instructions using imperative verbs (cut, mix, fold, press).
I can use signpost words to move between steps (first, next, after that, finally).
I can name each prop and describe size, shape, and amount.
frames: Today I will show you how to ___.

hs: I can tell a true story from my life using a story arc: hook, setting, build-up, turning point, resolution, and lesson.
I can use vivid details to show, not just tell, what happened.
I can share what the experience taught me and end with a memorable closing line.
col: I can shape a personal story around one clear theme and a turning point.
I can use sensory language and devices such as dialogue, repetition, and callback naturally.
I can connect my story’s insight to my audience and deliver it extemporaneously.

lang: I can use past-tense verbs and time words (first, then, suddenly, after that) to tell events in order.
I can use sensory words to describe what I saw, heard, and felt.
I can explain a lesson in the present tense (Now I…, Today I know…).

hs: I can take a clear side on a ProCon question and support it with three arguments.
I can use ethos, pathos, and logos, and spot weak reasoning (fallacies).
I can answer the strongest counterargument with evidence.
col: I can use Monroe’s Motivated Sequence to ask a real decision-maker to solve a local problem.
I can prove a need with local and peer-reviewed evidence and show my plan is feasible.
I can answer the strongest objection and end with a specific who/what/when ask.

lang: I can state a claim and give reasons using because, therefore, and for example.
I can respectfully disagree and rebut using contrast words (however, although, on the other hand).
I can use modal verbs to make a call to action (should, must, could).
